design.text: One-way, open-label, multicenter, two-phase study with a 6-month observational phase (OP) followed by a single-arm 12-month active treatment phase (ATP); no randomization, no blinding.

citations.quote: One-way, open-label, multicenter, 2-phase study of 6-month observational phase (OP), followed by single arm 1-year active treatment phase (ATP).

population.text: Adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older (≥35 kg) with severe hemophilia A without FVIII inhibitors or severe hemophilia B without FIX inhibitors.

citations.quote: The efficacy of HYMPAVZI was established in 116 adult and pediatric patients (aged 12 years and older and \ge 35 kg) with severe hemophilia A without FVIII inhibitors or severe hemophilia B without FIX inhibitors enrolled in the BASIS study (NCT03938792), an open-label, multi-center, two-phase study.

endpoint.text: Primary endpoint was the annualized bleeding rate (ABR) of treated bleeding events during HYMPAVZI treatment compared with the observational phase.

citations.quote: Primary: annualized bleeding rate (ABR) of treated bleeding events

n.text: 116 patients received HYMPAVZI (33 in the on-demand cohort, 83 in the routine prophylaxis cohort).

citations.quote: The efficacy of HYMPAVZI was established in 116 adult and pediatric patients
On-Demand Factor-Based Therapy During 6-Month OP (N = 33)	HYMPAVZI Prophylaxis During 12-Month ATP (N = 33)

result.text: Versus on-demand: treated-bleed ABR 3.18 (95% CI 2.09, 4.85) on HYMPAVZI vs 38.00 (31.03, 46.54); ratio 0.084 (0.059, 0.119), p<0.0001. Versus prior routine prophylaxis: treated-bleed ABR 5.08 (3.40, 6.77) vs 7.85 (5.09, 10.61); difference -2.77 (-5.37, -0.16), meeting non-inferiority.

indication.text: HYMPAVZI is a TFPI antagonist indicated for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency) without factor VIII inhibitors, or hemophilia B (congenital factor IX deficiency) without factor IX inhibitors.

citations.quote: HYMPAVZI is a tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI) antagonist indicated for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with:

- hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency) without factor VIII inhibitors, or
- hemophilia B (congenital factor IX deficiency) without factor IX inhibitors. (1)

target_moa.text: Marstacimab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody antagonist of tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI). It binds the Kunitz 2 (K2) domain of TFPI, neutralizing TFPI activity to enhance the extrinsic coagulation pathway and thrombin generation in patients with hemophilia.

citations.quote: Marstacimab-hncq is a human monoclonal IgG1 antibody directed against the Kunitz domain 2 (K2) of TFPI to neutralize TFPI activity and enhance coagulation.

key_safety.text: Adverse reactions reported in ≥3% of HYMPAVZI-treated patients (N=116) were injection site reaction 11 (9%), headache 8 (7%), and pruritus 4 (3%). Key warnings/precautions are thromboembolic events, hypersensitivity, and embryofetal toxicity.

- Thromboembolic Events: Thromboembolic events may occur. Interrupt HYMPAVZI prophylaxis if symptoms occur. (5.1)
- Hypersensitivity: Hypersensitivity reactions may occur. In the event of a severe allergic reaction, discontinue HYMPAVZI. (5.2)
- Embryofetal Toxicity: May cause fetal harm. Advise females of reproductive potential of the potential risk to the fetus and to use effective contraception. (5.3, 8.1, 8.3)

summary.text: BLA 761369 was a standard review (priority review requested but standard timeline applied). Marstacimab held orphan drug designation (May 18, 2016) and Fast Track Designation (September 17, 2019); a Breakthrough Therapy request was denied. Approval was based on the single pivotal BASIS study (B7841005) providing substantial evidence of effectiveness.

citations.quote: The application was set to be reviewed under a standard review timeline.

On May 18, 2016, marstacimab received orphan drug designation for treatment of Hemophilia A and Hemophilia B patients with or without inhibitors. Fast Track Designation was granted on September 17, 2019.

The Applicant submitted results from one adequate and well-controlled clinical study (Study B7841005) that served as the equivalent of two studies, which provides substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) of marstacimab for the indication.
